parts.note: the head, or first letter, of the word red is R
an egret is a white heron, a wading bird

explanation.surface: Someone pities a ginger-haired bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead' is read as red's head: its first letter R, not a ginger-haired person.
explanation.definitionFit: To regret something is to feel sorrow or remorse about it.

clue.text: Lager with no head? That is strange

indicators.note: the beer loses its head, so its opening letter is dropped

parts.note: lager is a kind of beer
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A drinker complains that a lager without froth is odd.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark pairs with 'head', the froth on a beer; 'with no head' removes its first letter, and 'That is' supplies the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means weird and unsettling, a synonym of strange.

parts.note: to rear children or animals is to train or bring them up
a range is a line or chain, as of mountains

explanation.surface: Instructions to move a train on to another line of track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' and 'train' both suggest railways; here 'train' is the verb rear, and 'on' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch things round is to change their order, a synonym.

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words Montmartre and more, running across the two

explanation.surface: In the Paris artists' quarter of Montmartre one feels a greater thrill.
explanation.definitionFit: A frisson is a shiver of excitement, a slight shaking or quiver.

clue.text: A purist's changed to a higher level

indicators.note: the letters of a purist's are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A purist has been promoted to a higher grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Going upstairs means going up to a higher floor of a building.

clue.text: Restrained by veto, Iran must end badly

indicators.note: the words veto, Iran must end are badly arranged, so their letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Diplomats were held back by a veto, and Iran's position must end in disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is only a link; 'badly' shuffles the fifteen letters of VETO IRAN MUST END.
explanation.definitionFit: An undemonstrative person keeps feelings in check, reserved and showing little emotion.

indicators.note: the letters of got and Asian become involved, mixed together into a new word

explanation.surface: Someone became entangled with a person from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges GOT plus ASIAN; 'with' only joins them. Santiago is the capital of Chile, not an Asian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Santiago is the capital city of Chile.

indicators.note: the leader of the word political is its first letter

parts.note: pal is an informal word for friend

explanation.surface: A party chief's so-called friend causes a public scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal someone is to shock and horrify them, as outrage does.

indicators.note: the back holds the other pieces within its grasp, so they go inside it

parts.note: the rear is the back of something
the gist is the heart or essence of a matter

explanation.surface: A doctor's back trouble is linked to the heart, on the right side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clutching' signals the container. A registrar is a British hospital doctor grade, so 'Doctor' is fair here.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a registrar is a grade of doctor below consultant.

clue.text: Mod a danger, possibly, for final conflict

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of mod a danger could form another word

explanation.surface: A Mod, perhaps a menace, ready for the last big fight, like the 1960s Mods and Rockers.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mod was a member of a 1960s British youth subculture who clashed with Rockers.
explanation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the biblical last battle between good and evil at the end of the world.

indicators.note: the frame holds the silver within it
the frame of a picture is its border, its first and last letters

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A picture frame with a silver leaf finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frame' takes P and E, the first and last letters of Picture; 'contains' puts AG between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf of a book is a sheet, each side of which is a page.

parts.note: an inherited treasure passed down through a family, made to sound like part of a family's valuables

explanation.definitionFit: An heirloom is a valued object handed down through generations of a family.

clue.text: Most frivolous setter would allow second entry

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I
'd is the short form of would, as in I'd

indicators.note: the second makes an entry into the word for allow

parts.note: to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A crossword setter claims they would permit a second, sillier answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter would' gives I'D; 'entry' puts S inside LET to make LEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can mean trivial or lacking purpose, so the idlest is the most trivial.

parts.note: the four bridge players are North, South, East and West; S is South
to pan is to criticise harshly, to slam

explanation.surface: A card game term: a bridge player's grand slam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slam' suggests the bridge term grand slam, but it means to criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is the arch or stretch of a bridge between supports.

indicators.note: the occupier comes after the power, so it follows it

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
a resident occupies a home

explanation.surface: A bush is invaded by someone who has taken charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Occupier is 'is'. 'Bush' is George Bush, a US head of state, not a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bush, father and son, both held the top office in the United States.

clue.text: Rev up a Conservative? It's pointless

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to rev an engine is to gun it
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Inspiring a Conservative is a waste of effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rev up' reads as a phrase about engines; 'up' is the reversal signal, and 'It's' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugatory means of no value or effect, futile.

clue.text: In RADA get parts for actor

indicators.note: the words in RADA get are broken into parts and reassembled

explanation.surface: At drama school students win roles to become actors.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, a London drama school.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an actor who specialises in tragic roles.

clue.text: Translation of dull epic's very clear

indicators.note: a translation renders the words dull epic in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive 's is read as is and adds no letter

explanation.surface: A rendering of a boring epic poem turns out to be very lucid.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of epic's is 'is', linking the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pellucid means transparently clear, in style or in water.

clue.text: Awed seeing queen in opening of royal show

indicators.note: the opening of royal is its first letter
the queen is put inside the word for show

parts.note: an event is a show or occasion
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone is overawed to see the Queen at the start of a royal gala.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container, and 'seeing' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent means showing deep respect, feeling awe or veneration.

clue.text: Gold ring initially has ace quality

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word ring

parts.note: A is short for ace in playing cards

explanation.surface: A gold ring has, at first sight, top-class quality.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is a distinctive atmosphere or character surrounding someone, an intangible quality.

parts.note: a con is a swindle, a robber's trick
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A thief's dog follows him about.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to agree, to accept another's view.

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

indicators.note: the word for charm loses its last letter

parts.note: a spell is a magic charm

explanation.surface: A peaceful young woman's lasting charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the final L of SPELL to leave SPEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel fears is to drive them away, to calm or allay them.

clue.text: Sometime ago had a type of Italian food?

parts.note: the past is a time gone by

explanation.surface: Long ago someone ate an Italian dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' only joins the pieces; the question mark flags the playful wording.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is a dough of flour and egg, a staple of Italian cooking.

parts.note: distressed is read as de-tressed, losing one's tresses or hair, not upset

explanation.definitionFit: Alopecia is a medical condition causing hair loss, leaving the scalp bare.

clue.text: House is grand with one toilet outside

indicators.note: the one and the toilet sit outside the grand, enclosing it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
loo is a British informal word for toilet
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A large house has a single outdoor lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts I and LOO round G. 'is' joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is an Inuit dwelling built of snow blocks.

clue.text: The French head of state's not so great

parts.note: les is the French plural form of the

indicators.note: the head of state is its first letter

explanation.surface: The French head of state is less impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of state' looks like a president; it is just the first letter of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Less means smaller in amount or degree, a lesser quantity.

indicators.note: the aloofness is seen inside the word for porcelain

parts.note: china is fine porcelain
a chill is coolness or aloofness of manner

explanation.surface: A cold manner is seen in a china cat ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat' at the end looks like part of the porcelain ornament but is the definition; 'seen in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The chinchilla is a breed of long-haired cat with a silver coat.

clue.text: Get on seat gripping bits of trace?

indicators.note: the seat grips the bits of trace, holding them within it

parts.note: a saddle is the seat a rider sits on
bits of trace are a part of the word, its opening letters T and R

explanation.surface: A rider mounts the saddle while holding parts of the harness traces.
explanation.walkthrough: Traces are the straps linking a horse to a cart, so the surface stays in the stable; 'gripping' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle a horse is to sit astride it, to mount or climb on.

indicators.note: the sprinted comes before the vault in order

parts.note: ran is past tense of run, to sprint

indicators.note: almost means the vault loses its final letter

parts.note: a dome is a vaulted roof

explanation.surface: A runner races ahead before a pole vault, almost out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims DOME to DOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Random means haphazard, without any guiding plan or control.
